data.name: Online_GuideTitle
data.value: Set up port forwarding on your router

data.name: Online_GuideWhy
data.value: Your router hides every device behind one public IP. Unless it is told which computer gets Minecraft traffic, it drops connections from outside, so friends cannot join with IP:port. PackCheck tries this automatically (UPnP); if the router does not allow it, add the rule yourself once.

data.name: Online_GuideValues
data.value: Enter exactly these values in the router

data.name: Online_Step0
data.value: Press "Open to the internet" above first: it allows the port in the Windows firewall (one administrator prompt). Router forwarding alone is not enough while the firewall blocks it.

data.name: Online_Step1
data.value: Open your router's page in a browser and sign in (the password is usually on a sticker under the router):

data.name: Online_Step2
data.value: Find the forwarding menu. Its name depends on the brand: Port Forwarding, NAT, Virtual Server, Port Mapping, Applications & Gaming (on many ISP routers it is under "Advanced", "Security" or "Firewall").

data.name: Online_Step3
data.value: Add a new rule with the values above and save. If the router asks for a port range, enter the same port as start and end.

data.name: Online_Step4
data.value: Give this PC a fixed local IP (DHCP reservation / "static lease" in the same router), otherwise the rule stops working when the IP changes after a restart.

data.name: Online_Step5
data.value: Start the server, then press "Test from outside" above. Green means friends can join with your public IP and port.

data.name: Online_CgnatTitle
data.value: CGNAT: when port forwarding cannot work

data.name: Online_CgnatDetected
data.value: PackCheck found signs of CGNAT on your connection. Read the steps below.

data.name: Online_CgnatWhat
data.value: Many providers no longer give each home its own internet (IPv4) address. With CGNAT (carrier-grade NAT) dozens of customers share one address, and your router only gets an internal one. Friends who connect to the shared address arrive at the provider, not at your home, so forwarding a port on your own router changes nothing. Nothing is wrong with your PC, PackCheck or your router settings.

data.name: Online_CgnatCheck
data.value: How to tell: open your router's page and find the WAN / Internet IP address. Compare it with the public IP shown at the top of this page. If they differ, or the router's address starts with 100.64 to 100.127 (shared provider range), 10., 172.16 to 172.31 or 192.168., you are behind CGNAT or behind a second router. A failing "Test from outside" after correct forwarding points to the same cause.

data.name: Online_CgnatFix1
data.value: 1. Ask your provider for a public IPv4 address. Call support and say: "I am behind CGNAT and need a public IPv4 address for port forwarding." Many providers switch you for free or for a small monthly fee (often sold as "static IP"). After the switch, restart the router and use "Open to the internet" again.

data.name: Online_CgnatFix2
data.value: 2. Use IPv6 if you and your friends have it. Java servers accept IPv6, and IPv6 addresses are not shared. Allow the port for IPv6 in the router's firewall, then give friends your PC's IPv6 address in brackets, e.g. [2a02:…]:25565. It only works for friends whose own connection has IPv6.

data.name: Online_CgnatFix3
data.value: 3. Use a tunnel: playit.gg (free, made for Minecraft). Create an account at playit.gg, download and run the playit program on this PC, add a "Minecraft Java" tunnel pointing to 127.0.0.1 and this server's port. playit gives you an address like name.joinmc.link that works from anywhere, no router changes needed. Keep playit running while you play.

data.name: Online_CgnatFix4
data.value: 4. For a few friends: a virtual LAN such as Tailscale, ZeroTier or Radmin VPN. You and every friend install the same program and join your network; friends then connect to your virtual address (e.g. 100.x.y.z:25565). Free and secure, but every player has to install it.

data.name: Online_CgnatFix5
data.value: 5. If none of this is possible, rent a small server (VPS) or a Minecraft host and run the server there; PackCheck's validation and pack checks still help you prepare it.

data.name: Online_CgnatDouble
data.value: Not CGNAT but two routers? If the router's WAN address is 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x and your provider's modem sits in front of it, you have double NAT. Forward the port on the provider's modem to your router, and on your router to this PC, or put the provider's modem into bridge mode.

data.name: Online_GuideTrouble
data.value: If it still does not work

data.name: Online_Trouble1
data.value: • CGNAT: if the router's WAN/Internet IP differs from the public IP above, forwarding cannot work. The CGNAT section below shows how to check it and what to do.

data.name: Online_Trouble2
data.value: • Two routers (ISP modem + your own Wi-Fi router): forward the port on both, or put the ISP modem in bridge mode.

data.name: Online_Trouble3
data.value: • Testing from your own network often fails because many routers do not support "hairpin" connections to their own public IP. Use the local address at home and let a friend (or the outside test) try the public one.

data.name: Online_Trouble4
data.value: • Your public IP can change; share a DuckDNS name (below) instead of the raw IP. Also make sure the server is running and online-mode/whitelist allow your friend.

data.value: Verify players with Mojang/Microsoft accounts. Turn off only behind an authenticating proxy.

data.name: Prop_enable-status
data.value: Appear online in the server list.

data.name: Prop_query.port
data.value: UDP port for the query protocol.

data.name: Prop_network-compression-threshold
data.value: Compress packets larger than this many bytes. -1 disables compression.

data.name: Prop_rate-limit
data.value: Kick players who send more packets per second. 0 disables it.

data.name: Prop_accepts-transfers
data.value: Accept players transferred from another server.

data.name: Prop_resource-pack
data.value: URL of a resource pack players are offered.

data.name: Prop_require-resource-pack
data.value: Kick players who decline the resource pack.

data.name: Prop_view-distance
data.value: How many chunks are sent to players (2–32). Higher costs more RAM and CPU.

data.name: Prop_simulation-distance
data.value: How many chunks around players are ticked (2–32).

data.name: Prop_entity-broadcast-range-percentage
data.value: How far entities are sent to clients, in percent of the default.

data.name: Prop_max-tick-time
data.value: Milliseconds a single tick may take before the watchdog stops the server. -1 disables it.

data.name: Prop_use-native-transport
data.value: Use optimized Linux networking when available.

data.name: Prop_max-chained-neighbor-updates
data.value: Limit of chained block updates in one tick. Negative disables it.

data.name: Prop_enforce-secure-profile
data.value: Require players to have a Mojang-signed public key for chat.

data.name: Prop_prevent-proxy-connections
data.value: Kick players whose IP differs from the one Mojang saw (blocks VPNs/proxies).

data.name: Prop_log-ips
data.value: Write player IP addresses to the log.

data.name: Prop_enable-rcon
data.value: Allow remote console access. Keep it off unless you need it.

data.name: Prop_rcon.password
data.value: Password for remote console. Use a long random one.

data.name: Prop_broadcast-rcon-to-ops
data.value: Show remote console output to online operators.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-monsters
data.value: Maximum hostile mobs per player area. Lower it to reduce lag.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-animals
data.value: Maximum passive animals per player area.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-water-animals
data.value: Maximum water animals (squid, dolphins) per player area.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-ambient
data.value: Maximum ambient mobs (bats) per player area.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-monster-spawns
data.value: Ticks between hostile spawn attempts (1 = every tick). Higher is lighter.

data.name: Prop_bukkit-connection-throttle
data.value: Milliseconds a player must wait between connection attempts (-1 = off, needed behind a proxy).

data.name: Prop_bukkit-allow-end
data.value: Whether the End dimension is enabled.

data.name: Prop_spigot-ear-animals
data.value: Blocks around players in which animals are fully ticked. Lower saves CPU.

data.name: Prop_spigot-ear-monsters
data.value: Blocks around players in which monsters are fully ticked.

data.name: Prop_spigot-ear-raiders
data.value: Blocks around players in which raiders are fully ticked.

data.name: Prop_spigot-ear-misc
data.value: Blocks around players in which other entities are fully ticked.

data.name: Prop_spigot-etr-players
data.value: Distance (blocks) at which other players are sent to a client.

data.name: Prop_spigot-etr-animals
data.value: Distance (blocks) at which animals are sent to a client.

data.name: Prop_spigot-etr-monsters
data.value: Distance (blocks) at which monsters are sent to a client.

data.name: Prop_spigot-timeout
data.value: Seconds without a tick before the watchdog reports the server as frozen.

data.name: Prop_spigot-restart-on-crash
data.value: Run the restart script when the server crashes.

data.name: Prop_spigot-bungeecord
data.value: Enable when the server runs behind a BungeeCord/Velocity (legacy) proxy.

data.name: Prop_paper-autosave-chunks
data.value: Maximum chunks saved per tick during autosave. Lower smooths lag spikes.

data.name: Prop_paper-entity-collisions
data.value: Maximum collisions an entity checks per tick. Lower helps mob farms.

data.name: Prop_paper-spawner-tick
data.value: How often mob spawners tick (1 = every tick). 2 halves their cost.

data.name: Prop_paper-armor-stands-tick
data.value: Whether armor stands tick. Turn off to save CPU if no plugin needs it.

data.name: Prop_paper-hopper-move-event
data.value: Skip the hopper move event (big speed-up, but breaks plugins that listen to it).

data.name: Prop_paper-prevent-unloaded
data.value: Stop players from moving into chunks that are not loaded yet.

data.name: Prop_paper-max-joins
data.value: Players that may join per tick; limits join floods.
